units.jupiter_glb: jupiter_*.glb has radius 1 = 1 Jupiter equatorial radius (R_J = 71,492 km).
units.moon_glbs: io.glb, europa.glb, ganymede.glb, callisto.glb each have radius 1 = that moon's mean radius. Scale them by (moon_radius_km / R_J_km) to place them next to Jupiter.
units.mars_glb: mars_*.glb has radius 1 = 1 Mars equatorial radius (3,396.2 km).
units.sun_glb: sun.glb has radius 1 = 1 solar equatorial radius (695,700 km).
units.earth_in_kepler: For Sun-centered Kepler views, reuse earth_*.glb (radius 1 = R_E). Scale by (R_E_km / R_sun_km) = 6380/695700 relative to sun.glb if you ever need true body scale. For the eccentricity comparison, enlarge the planets and the comet; mark them not to scale.
units.comet_glb: comet.glb is 1P/Halley-style icy nucleus. 1 unit = 1 km. The nucleus is about 11 km across (NASA). Optional mesh dust_tail is hideable, non-emissive, and not to scale. Point any tail away from the Sun in the app.
units.stopper_glb: stopper.glb is a lab-style rubber stopper for the L2 circular-motion / cut-the-string demo. 1 unit = 1 meter. The stopper is about 0.03 m in radius. Empty string_attach marks the string connection. Do not add an outward (centrifugal) force arrow.
units.sun_at_one_focus: Place the Sun at the origin (one focus). The geometric center of an ellipse is at (-a*e, 0) if perihelion is on the +X axis. Perihelion is then at (a*(1-e), 0) and aphelion at (-a*(1+e), 0). The other focus is at (-2*a*e, 0) and must stay empty. There is no object at the second focus.

Europa.notes: Tidally locked. Nearly circular; the 1:2:4 resonance with Io and Ganymede keeps a small eccentricity.

Ganymede.notes: Largest moon in the solar system. Tidally locked. Nearly circular.

Callisto.notes: Tidally locked. Not part of the Io-Europa-Ganymede resonance. Nearly circular.

moon_radii_source_note: Diameters (Io 3643, Europa 3122, Ganymede 5262, Callisto 4821 km) are from the NASA NSSDC Solar System Small Worlds Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/galileanfact_table.html. Mean radii are half those diameters (Ganymede 2631.2 km matches the commonly cited value).

mars.notes: The lesson uses e=0.093 to show that Mars is only slightly elliptical, not a stretched oval. Perihelion and aphelion here are a(1-e) and a(1+e) with e=0.093 and a=227.956 million km, which students can plot around the Sun. NSSDC quotes e=0.0934 and slightly different peri/aph.
mars.name: Mars

sun_at_origin_placement.description: Sun at (0,0). Perihelion along +X. The second focus is empty.

teaching_notes.orbits_nearly_circular: All four Galilean eccentricities are <0.01. Most student textbooks overdraw ellipses; keep these orbits visually circular and use Mars at e=0.093 as the slightly-stretched example.
teaching_notes.resonance: Io, Europa, and Ganymede are in a 1:2:4 mean-motion resonance (periods 1.77, 3.55, 7.15 days).
teaching_notes.sun_not_at_center: The Sun sits at one focus, not at the center of the ellipse. The other focus is empty.
teaching_notes.no_outward_force: The L2 circular-motion demo must never depict an outward (centrifugal) force. The real force is inward. After the inward pull is removed, the path is a straight tangent.

earth.name: Earth

sun_at_origin_placement.description: Sun at (0,0). Perihelion along +X. The second focus is empty.

earth.notes: The lesson uses e=0.017. NSSDC lists 0.0167. By eye this orbit is indistinguishable from a circle. Source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html

halley.name: 1P/Halley

sun_at_origin_placement.description: Sun at (0,0). Perihelion along +X. The second focus is empty.

halley.notes: NASA NSSDC Comet Fact Sheet values: period 76.1 years, perihelion 0.587 AU, semi-major axis 17.94 AU, eccentricity 0.967, inclination 162.2 deg (retrograde). https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/cometfact.html. The widely used 'about 17.8 AU' is a rounded figure; this file uses the NSSDC 17.94 AU. q=a(1-e)=0.592 AU is slightly above the tabulated perihelion 0.587 AU because a and e are rounded in the table. For the Lesson 3 comparison, draw a planar ellipse (ignore the 162 deg tilt) so students can see the shape. Nucleus diameter about 11 km: https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/comets/1p-halley/. The other focus is empty.

lesson_presets.L2_S5_cut_the_string: Circular path with velocity tangent and force (or acceleration) inward, toward the center. Use stopper.glb (or a generic orbiting mass). Include a 'cut the inward pull' action so the object goes straight along the tangent (path C). Never draw an outward / centrifugal force. If there were an outward force, path A would happen, and it does not.
lesson_presets.L3_S6_eccentricity: Starting state: Earth's orbit (e=0.017) and 1P/Halley's orbit (e=0.967, a=17.94 AU) to scale, with the Sun at one focus and the other focus empty. Also show Mars (e=0.093) if available. Earth looks like a circle by eye; Mars is only slightly oval; the comet is the clearly stretched path. Planet and comet bodies should be enlarged and marked not to scale; the orbits are to scale with each other.
lesson_presets.jupiter_moons: Galilean moons around Jupiter, nearly circular, for later Kepler work (Io period, T^2 vs a^3).
